title: Downhill Domination
subtitle: The whole mountain becomes a racecourse
summary: Downhill Domination is Incog Inc. Entertainment's PlayStation 2 mountain-bike racing game, first released in North America on 22 July 2003. body: Downhill Domination is Incog Inc. Entertainment's PlayStation 2 mountain-bike racing game, first released in North America on 22 July 2003. Riders descend large courses at exaggerated speed, taking jumps and exchanging blows while trying to reach the finish first. The mountain offers room to choose a line rather than keeping everyone inside a narrow circuit. A shortcut may promise an advantage while bringing a more difficult landing. The game's arcade approach turns downhill riding into a mixture of route finding, spectacle and the immediate problem of staying ahead of another cyclist.

The player has to read the slope ahead while managing speed, jumps and nearby rivals. Tricks add another reason to leave the ground, but a good-looking movement still needs a safe landing if the descent is to continue. Contact with opponents makes the surrounding race more than background scenery. Career progression opens more riders and equipment, while repeated attempts reveal where the terrain offers a better route. The same mountain gradually becomes easier to read, allowing the player to commit to a line earlier and carry more speed through it.

The initial cast of invented riders is joined by unlockable professionals, including Eric Carter, Tara Llanes, Brian Lopes, Richie Schley and Missy Giove. Their presence connects the exaggerated action to downhill cycling beyond the game. Scott Campbell directed and designed the project for Incog, with Sony publishing in North America and Codemasters bringing it to Europe in 2004. Multiplayer makes the descent a shared competition. Its identity comes from enlarging the sport's dangers into an arcade race while retaining the basic excitement of choosing a path down a mountain at speed.
